articles.title: How Intelligence Agencies Bend Universities to Their Will
articles.author: Hager Ben Jaffel
articles.content_excerpt: With a series of US military operations underway over the past year, intelligence agencies have come under the spotlight again. Media coverage has tended to offer flattering narratives of their exploits, recounting the “ critical role ” played by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) in Nicolás Maduro’s kidnapping that makes it seem like a spy thriller . This fits into a wider tendency during the Trump era to repackage US power as a form of entertainment, drawing on action movies and video games to turn imperialist ventures into thrilling adventures. At the same time, former intelligence practitioners and professional associations have lamented the politicization of intelligence under the Trump administration, warning of its disastrous consequences for US national security. articles.title: Americans Are Turning to GoFundMe Just to Get By
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: At this point, you have to have been trapped in space for the last two years not to notice that the cost of living is onerously high. Or you could just be the Treasury secretary . In any case, there’s no shortage of metrics that show Americans are struggling: rising credit card delinquencies , a spike in foreclosure filings , surging demand for food banks, or the growing number of high-income Americans deciding to shop at budget stores like Dollar Tree. Alternatively, you could just look at GoFundMe. articles.title: The Killer AI Robots Are Already Here
articles.author: Robert Sparrow
articles.content_excerpt: Over the last few weeks, panic about artificial intelligence has reached a fever pitch. AI industry whistleblowers as well as politicians like Bernie Sanders are sounding the alarm about the potential for an AI-driven apocalypse and the need to slow down or pause further development of the technology. But lest we forget, AI is in fact already killing human beings, thanks to the increasing deployment of autonomous weapons systems in warfare. A recent high-profile incident, covered by the New York Times last month, saw three Ukrainian civilians killed by an AI-guided drone. An AI system has also infamously been used to select targets in Israel’s genocidal assault on Gaza. articles.title: The Uprising Wastes a Good Class-Struggle Story
articles.author: Jeremy Gong
articles.content_excerpt: In 1381, more than a hundred thousand poor English people rose up demanding an end to serfdom. During the uprising, they killed a coterie of hated government officials, and, in turn, the fourteen-year-old King Richard II massacred thousands of them. The best-remembered figure of the English Peasants’ Revolt is one of its leaders, John Ball, whose speeches and sermons captured the spirit of what would eventually, centuries later, develop into socialism. “When Adam delved and Eve span, who was then the gentleman?” he famously asked, meaning that in the Garden of Eden, the Bible’s first people labored only for their own sustenance, with no concepts of lords and serfs. articles.title: The Prospects for a 2028 May Day Mass Strike
articles.author: Luis Feliz Leon
articles.content_excerpt: Three years ago, the United Auto Workers (UAW), glowing with confidence after a successful strike at the Big Three and pledging ambitious new organizing drives, put out a call for a national strike on May 1, 2028. UAW President Shawn Fain called for unions to align their contracts with the Big Three to build leverage and create a crisis for the billionaire class. It was a new day in the UAW, and a wider labor renewal felt possible. May 2028 is now only a year and a half away. Are unions getting in gear for a season of strikes and labor action around then, as contracts expire in manufacturing, education, logistics, grocery, and the building trades? Some are.
